name: 93. Provider error messages survive the borrowed Bedrock handlers (bedrock-error-message)
description: bedrock-runtime reports failures on its native APIs (Converse and InvokeModel) in AWS's own flat shape, {"message":"...","__type":"..."}, not in the error envelope the Anthropic and OpenAI wire formats use. That matters on the InvokeModel path, taken when a tool carries defer_loading, or for tool_search / context_management on Anthropic-family models (see folder 71): the request and response bodies are served by anthropic.HandleAnthropicResponsesStream, whose ParseAnthropicError reads only the nested {"type":"error","error":{...}} envelope, so error.message came back empty and the logs UI rendered no error at all while the reason survived only in the raw response. HandleProviderAPIError now seeds the message from a root-level "message" before the caller's own parser runs, and these cases pin that the reason the provider gave is the reason the caller is told. Bedrock's OpenAI-compatible surfaces (bedrock_openai_ep and Bedrock Mantle) are deliberately not covered here: they answer in the OpenAI envelope, which ParseOpenAIError already reads, so a case there cannot demonstrate the regression. The trigger is an out-of-range temperature, which AWS rejects with a ValidationException; each row is tagged [EXPECT-4XX] so the collection-level status test asserts the upstream rejection instead of requiring a 200, and if that temperature ever stops being rejected, that tag is what fails. The assertions compare against extra_fields.raw_response rather than AWS wording, so they survive a change in the text.

pm.expect(/^provider API error/i.test(message), 'error.message is a generic placeholder, not the reason the provider gave: ' + message).to.be.false;

var providerMessage = raw && typeof raw === 'object' && typeof raw.message === 'string' ? raw.message : '';

pm.test('bedrock invoke /v1/responses: error.message carries what the provider actually said', function () {
